prompt: You want to wrap a $3 \times 3 \times 3$ cube. How much paper (in cm²) do you need?
hint: The paper has to cover the outside of the cube. Is that a question about volume or about surface area?

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Think of wrapping one side at a time. You cover one square, then another, until every side of the cube is covered.
The paper has to cover the outside of the cube. Is that a question about volume or about surface area?
Each face is $3 \times 3 = 9$ square centimeters, and there are $6$ faces to cover. Multiply to get the total.
$6 \times 9 = 54$, so you need $54$ square centimeters of paper.

explanation: Wrapping paper covers the outside of the cube, so the amount needed is the surface area.
Each face is a square with side $3$, so one face has area $3 \times 3 = 9$.
The cube has $6$ faces, which gives $SA = 6 \times 9 = 54$.
You need $54$ square centimeters of paper to wrap the cube.
